subject.title: feat(agents): agent-controlled session status, attention, and TTL in the sessions tool

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-controlled, persisted sidebar status and attention as part of the permanent model-facing `sessions.patch` contract?
rationale: This is a new user-visible agent capability with new gateway parameters and session-state lifecycle semantics; test coverage can validate an accepted design but cannot choose the permanent product and protocol boundary.

options.title: Accept the scoped session-presence contract
options.body: Keep the three additive parameters and the bounded, self-clearing session status model after live behavior proof confirms the intended lifecycle.

options.title: Narrow to automatic attention only
options.body: Decline agent-declared attention/status and retain the existing queue-, approval-, and error-derived sidebar attention states.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped session-presence contract
recommendation.body: Keep the three additive parameters and the bounded, self-clearing session status model after live behavior proof confirms the intended lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature builds directly on the sidebar attention and narration behavior introduced in this person’s earlier merged work.
